title: VS Code Hook Wire Output
description: VS Code-native wire shape emitted by the Python controller for a hook event (spec015 Task 8.2). This is a SEPARATE contract from decision-output.schema.v1.json (the internal allow|deny|ask vocabulary). It models the three native output families: permission (PreToolUse: hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision), block (PostToolUse/Stop/SubagentStop: top-level decision='block' + reason), and common (SessionStart/SubagentStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreCompact: continue/stopReason/systemMessage). The token 'deny' is NOT a permitted top-level decision value here: emitting a bare top-level {"decision":"deny"} for a PreToolUse event fails OPEN in VS Code and is the cardinal sin this schema rejects. The only legal top-level decision value is 'block'. UNRECOGNIZED EVENTS: an unrecognized or non-string hookEventName is handled fail-closed as a cross-family deny — the adapter emits BOTH a top-level decision='block' AND hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision='deny', and deliberately OMITS continue=false (which would brick the human chat) — so a deny is honored whichever native family the unknown event belongs to.

permissionDecision.description: PreToolUse permission family verdict. 'deny' here is event-scoped (denies the single tool call); it is NOT the forbidden top-level 'deny'.

decision.description: Top-level block-family verdict. 'block' is the ONLY legal value; 'deny' here fails open and is rejected by this schema.

continue.description: Common/block behavioral modifier. continue=false signals a non-recoverable stop (session MUST NOT continue).

allOf.$comment: A top-level decision='block' MUST carry a reason.
